transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, since I stopped working, I just can’t seem to slow down. I’m up and moving all day, going from one little job to the next, like I still have a crew waiting on me or something. It’s wearing on me some, and I figured I ought to talk to someone about it.
When this happens, do you feel like you need less sleep than usual?
I don’t think so, no. I mean, I still need my sleep about the same as usual. I might be restless during the day, but I haven’t noticed needing less sleep.
Do you get upsetting thoughts that keep popping into your mind and make you feel driven to do these little jobs?
No, I wouldn’t say that. It’s not like a thought gets stuck in my head and I have to do it to feel better. I just notice something that needs doing, and then I’m off doing it.
Growing up, did you often have trouble paying attention or staying focused?

Yeah, I did. Even back in grade school, teachers would say I was bright enough, but kind of scattered. I was always losing pencils and things, blurting out answers, and they had to remind me to finish my work before I ran out to recess.
As an adult, do you still often have trouble staying focused or organized?

Yes, I do. It’s not terrible all the time, but I get pulled off pretty easily. Like if I’m trying to paint or plan out a story and I hear a truck outside, or I suddenly think of something I should do in the garden, my mind just jumps over there. Then when I come back, I’ve lost where I was.
Before age 12, were you often fidgety or unable to stay seated when you were expected to?

I don’t remember every detail, but yeah, in grade school I was definitely seen as scattered. Teachers said I was bright, but I was always losing pencils, calling out answers, and needing reminders to finish my work before recess.
Did this feeling of being unable to slow down start only after you stopped working?

No, not only after I stopped working. It’s just more noticeable now. Since I stopped working, I feel like I still can’t slow down—I’m up and moving from one little job to the next all day, almost like there’s still a crew waiting on me.
Do these focus or restlessness problems cause trouble in more than one part of your life, like at home and in social situations?

Yes. At home my wife has pretty much had to take over the calendar, and she checks behind me on things because I’ll miss something or forget what I said I’d do. And socially, or with groups, I’ve had to apologize to the community center and the garden group more than once for letting people down. It’s not constant disaster, but it does cause problems.
When you find yourself constantly moving from one task to another, is it usually because you’re worrying a lot?
Not usually, no. It’s more like I just can’t settle down since I stopped working. I’ll go from one little job to the next all day, almost like I still have people waiting on me to get things done.
